stories.teaser: A plant-based food from local crops to treat child malnutrition
stories.headline: Hebrew University researchers develop a plant-based malnutrition treatment made from locally grown crops
stories.why: Published in Current Developments in Nutrition; promising results in rats, with clinical trials still needed.
texts:
Treating malnutrition with what grows nearby.

Hebrew University researchers led by Dr. Aurélie Bechoff developed ChSMS, a therapeutic food made from chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean instead of imported powdered milk and peanuts. In a study in rats, it supported better recovery than a commercial formula.

“Access is one of the biggest challenges in treating childhood malnutrition,” says Prof. Efrat Monsonego-Ornan.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition

Only about 30% of children who need treatment for severe acute malnutrition receive it.

A Hebrew University team wants to change that with a ready-to-use therapeutic food made from local crops: chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean. It gets about 14% of its energy from protein, versus 10% for a commercial product, with a protein quality score of 87% versus 69%. The early results come from rats; clinical trials are still needed.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition

What if malnutrition treatment didn’t depend on imported milk powder?

Researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem tested a plant-based alternative made from chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean. In rats, it supported catch-up growth and better recovery than a peanut-and-milk formula. The findings, published in Current Developments in Nutrition, still need confirmation in clinical trials.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition
stories.source_name: American Friends of the Hebrew University, Oct 19, 2026
stories.og_title: Could locally grown crops make malnutrition treatment more accessible worldwide?

stories.teaser: A 99-million-year-old insect named after a Teletubbies vacuum cleaner
stories.headline: Tel Aviv University researchers describe “Noo-Noo,” a 99-million-year-old insect with an extraordinary feeding tube
stories.why: A new species found in amber, published in the journal Insects.
texts:
Meet “Noo-Noo.”

Tel Aviv University researchers have described a new planthopper species preserved in amber about 99 million years old. Its mouthparts were nearly twice the length of its body, likely flexible enough to reach sap deep in cracks of tree bark. The name honors the friendly vacuum cleaner from Teletubbies, whose hose looks a lot like it.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science

“This is not merely an insect previously unknown to science, but an animal that developed an evolutionary solution with almost no modern equivalent…” says Dr. Leonidas-Romanos Davranoglou of Tel Aviv University.

His team, led with Dolev Fabrikant, examined 13 amber specimens and used micro-CT scans to reconstruct a feeding tube nearly twice the insect’s body length. Published in the journal Insects.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science

What did insects eat in the age of the dinosaurs?

A Tel Aviv University team found a new species in 99-million-year-old amber, with mouthparts nearly twice its body length. They believe it was a sap-sucking specialist that reached deep into tree bark. They named it Cretodorus noonoo, after the vacuum cleaner from Teletubbies.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science
stories.og_title: Meet “Noo-Noo”: A 99-Million-Year-Old Insect with a Surprising Secret

stories.teaser: Ketamine’s pain relief may not need its mind-altering effect
stories.headline: Tel Aviv University study finds ketamine’s pain relief is separate from its mind-altering effects
stories.why: A brain-imaging study of 37 volunteers, published in Neuropsychopharmacology.
texts:
Pain relief without feeling detached?

Researchers from Tel Aviv University and Tel Aviv Medical Center (Ichilov) found that ketamine’s pain-relieving effect is separate from the dissociation it can cause. In 37 healthy volunteers, stronger dissociation didn’t mean more pain relief. This could point to treatments that keep the relief while reducing the side effects.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #PainRelief #Neuroscience

Does ketamine have to change how you feel to relieve pain? A new Israeli study suggests not.

A team led by Dr. Noam Goldway, with Prof. Talma Hendler and Dr. Haggai Sharon of Tel Aviv University, scanned the brains of 37 volunteers given ketamine and a placebo. Pain relief and dissociation showed up in different brain networks. Published in Neuropsychopharmacology.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #PainRelief #Neuroscience

Two effects, two different brain networks.

Using fMRI scans, Tel Aviv University researchers found that ketamine’s pain relief was linked to reduced activity in the insula and anterior cingulate cortex, while its dissociative effect involved the brain’s default mode network. People with little dissociation could still benefit. The study involved 37 healthy volunteers.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #PainRelief #Neuroscience
stories.og_title: Can Ketamine Relieve Pain Without Altering Consciousness?

stories.teaser: Israel’s 11th university opens in the Galilee
stories.headline: Tel-Hai University opens in Kiryat Shmona as Israel’s 11th university
stories.why: A northern college becomes a university, with about 5,000 students and plans to grow to 8,000.
texts:
Israel has a new university.

Tel-Hai Academic College in the Galilee has officially become Tel-Hai University of Kiryat Shmona, Israel’s 11th university. About 5,000 students are enrolled, and the plan is to grow to 8,000 over five years.

“We are not just establishing an academic institution; we are building a strategic national and social anchor,” says university president Dr. Eliezer Shalev.

#Israel #Galilee #HigherEducation #TelHai

A plan first drafted in 2005 came true this week.

Tel-Hai University of Kiryat Shmona opened as Israel’s 11th university, near the country’s northernmost city. Its faculty is expected to double from 150 to 300 over five years, across social sciences and humanities, life and environmental sciences, education, and engineering and advanced computing.

#Israel #Galilee #HigherEducation #TelHai

A university at the top of the map.

Israel’s 11th university has opened in Kiryat Shmona, in the Galilee. Enrollment at Tel-Hai University is back to about 5,000 students, and about 70% of them come from outside the region.

“We don’t see ourselves as a university that just happens to be located somewhere and is teaching,” says Prof. Eyal Shimoni.

#Israel #Galilee #HigherEducation #TelHai
stories.og_title: New university opens near Israel’s northernmost city, hoping to boost war-battered region

stories.teaser: Immigrants honored for what they’ve given Israel
stories.headline: Nefesh B’Nefesh honors eight immigrants with the Bonei Zion Prize
stories.why: Honorees include the inventor of the Alzheimer’s drug Exelon and the founder of Beit Issie Shapiro.
texts:
They came from abroad and built something here.

At the 12th Nefesh B’Nefesh Sylvan Adams Bonei Zion Prize ceremony in Jerusalem, eight immigrants from English-speaking countries were honored. Among them: pharmacologist Marta Weinstock-Rosin, inventor of the Alzheimer’s drug Exelon, and Naomi Stuchiner, founder of Beit Issie Shapiro.

“Israel’s single greatest strength is its people,” says Sylvan Adams.

#Israel #Aliyah #BoneiZion #NefeshBNefesh

A pharmacologist, an educator, a sports leader and a YouTuber.

These are some of the immigrants honored at this year’s Nefesh B’Nefesh Bonei Zion Prize in Jerusalem. The eight winners include Marta Weinstock-Rosin, who invented the Alzheimer’s drug Exelon, Rabbanit Chana Henkin, founder of Nishmat, Ami Baran, president of the Israel Athletics Association, and Barak Swarttz, founder of GRIT for Good.

#Israel #Aliyah #BoneiZion #NefeshBNefesh

“Israel’s single greatest strength is its people,” says Sylvan Adams.

The Nefesh B’Nefesh Bonei Zion Prize, held for the 12th time at the Jerusalem Theater, honored eight immigrants from English-speaking countries, in fields from science and medicine to education, sports and young leadership. Lifetime Achievement went to Marta Weinstock-Rosin, inventor of the Alzheimer’s drug Exelon.

#Israel #Aliyah #BoneiZion #NefeshBNefesh
stories.og_title: Nefesh B’Nefesh awards 8 immigrants for exceptional contributions to Israel

stories.teaser: AI helps hospitalized children who can’t speak communicate
stories.headline: Schneider Children’s Medical Center launches an AI tool that helps children who can’t speak communicate
stories.why: Personalized communication boards now take under five minutes to make, instead of hours.
texts:
Giving children their voice back.

Schneider Children’s Medical Center and Code for Israel launched an AI tool that creates personalized communication boards for hospitalized children who can’t speak. Boards that took hours to prepare now take under five minutes.

“The story is restoring children’s ability to communicate, express themselves, and participate actively in their care,” says Dr. Oshrat Sella Weiss.

#Israel #Schneider #AI #ChildrensHealth

Under five minutes, instead of several hours.

That’s how long it now takes to make a personalized communication board for a child at Schneider Children’s Medical Center who can’t speak, whether because of a ventilator, a language difficulty, or being too young or weak to write. The new AI tool tailors each board to the child’s age, language and background.

#Israel #Schneider #AI #ChildrensHealth

“For us, technology is not the story,” says Dr. Oshrat Sella Weiss of Schneider Children’s Medical Center.

The story is children on ventilators, or too weak to write, who can now point to a board made just for them. Created with Code for Israel, the AI tool builds these boards in minutes, and teams can update and share them.

#Israel #Schneider #AI #ChildrensHealth
stories.og_title: Israeli hospital launches AI system to help hospitalized children communicate

stories.teaser: A 3D-printed cornea implant helped a blind eye see again
stories.headline: A bioprinted cornea implant, transplanted in Israel, restored sight to a patient’s blind eye
stories.why: Five patients have received Precise Bio’s implant at Rambam; trial results are expected in 2027.
texts:
Printed tissue, restored sight.

At Rambam Health Care Campus, a patient who was blind in one eye regained vision after receiving a bioprinted corneal implant made with live cells by Precise Bio. Five patients have received the implant so far, and trial results are expected in 2027.

“So we proved that it is no longer science fiction,” says founder Aryeh Batt.

#Israel #Rambam #Bioprinting #Vision

He was told his idea was science fiction.

Physicist Aryeh Batt co-founded Precise Bio to print living corneal tissue. Now five patients have received its implant at Rambam Health Care Campus, with surgeons from Shaare Zedek and Beilinson. The first patient, blind in the treated eye, regained vision in that eye.

“The cornea is the first. I promise you it will not be the last.”

#Israel #Rambam #Bioprinting #Vision

One donor, hundreds of patients?

Precise Bio says it can produce 400 to 500 bioprinted corneal implants from a single donor. The implant replaces the cornea’s inner layer, and in the first transplant at Rambam, a patient who was blind in that eye regained vision. Its trial is planned for 15 patients, with results expected in 2027.

#Israel #Rambam #Bioprinting #Vision
stories.og_title: He was told his idea was science fiction: Now the tissue he printed restored people's sight

stories.teaser: Israeli climber Yonatan Katz wins Boulder World Cup gold
stories.headline: Israel’s Yonatan Katz wins gold at the final Boulder World Cup of 2026
stories.why: Only the second Israeli climber ever to win a World Climbing Series medal.
texts:
Gold on the final boulder.

Israeli climber Yonatan Katz won the men’s final at the last Boulder World Cup of 2026 in Salt Lake City, topping the final boulder on his fourth attempt. He is only the second Israeli climber in any discipline to win a World Climbing Series medal.

“I just turned off my brain, went for it, and managed to grab the jug,” he says.

#Israel #Climbing #YonatanKatz #IsraeliSport

“My goal was never to just participate in a final it was to compete in one,” says Yonatan Katz.

He did more than compete. In only his second World Climbing Series final, the Israeli climber won gold at the Boulder World Cup in Salt Lake City with 69.7 points, ahead of Great Britain’s Max Milne and Japan’s Rei Kawamata. Israel’s Or Mark finished sixth in his first-ever final.

#Israel #Climbing #YonatanKatz #IsraeliSport

He was behind going into the last climb.

Then Israel’s Yonatan Katz topped the final boulder on his fourth attempt to win gold at the Boulder World Cup in Salt Lake City. It was only his second World Climbing Series final.

“I don’t know how it feels, it’s probably going to take a while to sink in,” he says.

#Israel #Climbing #YonatanKatz #IsraeliSport
stories.og_title: Israeli Climber Yonatan Katz Wins Gold in USA

stories.teaser: Israeli scientists upgrade the immune system’s cancer-fighting cells
stories.headline: Bar-Ilan and Weizmann researchers engineer stronger immune cells that shrank tumors in mice
stories.why: Published in Science Advances; preclinical results, with clinical trials the next goal.
texts:
Upgrading the immune system’s scouts.

Researchers from Bar-Ilan University and the Weizmann Institute redesigned the receptor T cells use to recognize cancer. In mice with tumors from human cancer cells, tumors treated with the improved cells were about 35% smaller after 83 days. The results are preclinical, and the team plans to move toward clinical trials.

#Israel #BarIlan #Weizmann #CancerResearch

All the mice that received the improved cells were still alive on day 127, compared with fewer than half in the control group.

Prof. Ciril Cohen of Bar-Ilan and Prof. Sarel Fleishman of the Weizmann Institute used computational protein design to build a stronger T-cell receptor called SET. It’s early, preclinical work, published in Science Advances.

#Israel #BarIlan #Weizmann #CancerResearch

“Another piece in the big puzzle of the war against cancer,” says Prof. Ciril Cohen of Bar-Ilan University.

His team, with Weizmann Institute researchers, engineered T cells that killed cancer cells better in the lab and shrank tumors in mice. The same approach also improved T cells aimed at melanoma targets and viruses. Further studies are needed before it reaches patients.

#Israel #BarIlan #Weizmann #CancerResearch
stories.og_title: הגידולים הצטמקו: חוקרים ישראלים שדרגו את "הסיירת" של מערכת החיסון
